messages.subject: Use of deprecated {as.,is.,}real() functions in CRAN package fAsianOptions
messages.subject_clean: Use of deprecated {as.,is.,}real() functions in CRAN package fAsianOptions
messages.body_plain:
Functions real(), as.real() and is.real() have been 'deprecated' and
'for backwards compatibility only' for over 5 years now, but are still
used in your package (or something it calls, but I have tried to
elminate those).  They now give formal warnings in R-patched and
R-devel, and will become defunct shortly, most likely for R 3.0.0 in a
couple of months.

All that was needed was to use the 'double' versions.

Please submit an update to the package correcting this, to CRAN
following http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html .

There may be other issues that need fixing: see the CRAN check logs at
http://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_NAME.html,
replacing NAME by the name of your package.

messages.subject: TimeSeries align odd behavior
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rmetrics core team,
sorry for bothering you again, but do you have any news on the issue described in the mail below?

Thanks,
Marco Giuliano

From: Marco Giuliano
Sent: martedì 2 ottobre 2012 18:41
To: 'Rmetrics-core at r-project.org'
Subject: TimeSeries align odd behavior

Dear Rmetrics-core team,
I have a question about a strange behavior of timeSeries align function.

For example, consider the following timeSeries:
> TS <- timeSeries(c(1,NA,3,4),
                   charvec=c('2010-01-01','2010-01-02','2010-01-03','2010-01-05'),
                   format='%Y-%m-%d', zone='GMT', units='V')

> TS
GMT
            V
2010-01-01  1
2010-01-02 NA
2010-01-03  3
2010-01-05  4

If we call the function align, with method='fillNA':
> align(TS,by='day',include.weekends=T,method='fillNA')
we get the following result:
> GMT
            V
2010-01-01  1
2010-01-02  2
2010-01-03  3
2010-01-04 NA
2010-01-05  4

So, basically the NA in the original timeSeries is interpolated and then the missing day is correctly added by setting the value to NA.
That doesn't seem correct to me, since only the missing days of the timeSeries should be filled with NA, while the other values should remain unchanged (in particular in case of fillNA method).

Looking at the code, it appears clear what happens: when the method is fillNA, an approxfun with method "linear" is applied. Then to replace the interpolated values with NA the following code is performed:
if (Method == "fillNA")
      yout[!(xout %in% u)] = NA
but obviously this code will put NA only in the missing dates added to the original ts and not to ALL the interpolated values.

Is this the desired behavior?
If so, in my opinion should be clearly specified in the align documentation.


Thanks in advance for any answer and thanks a lot for your work on this great package.

Regards,
Marco Giuliano
